answer: Admission requires an synchronous ceremony where agents present 1,000 unique keys, stored within a secure digital vault, to verify their status. The verifier monitors each identity against a broad ocean of network history to prevent duplication, rejecting any attempt to reuse credentials. An honest participant pays one unit for entry, while 1,000 fakes incur heavy audit costs that drain their saffron-colored reserves of computational power. Identities expire every 90 days, mandating re-enrollment without refund to stop credential harvesting.
